title: Kth Smallest Element in a Sorted Matrix
summary: Find the k^th smallest element in an n x n matrix with sorted rows and columns, using less than O(n^2) memory.
statement: Find the k^th smallest element in an n x n matrix with sorted rows and columns, using less than O(n^2) memory.
constraints: The square matrix has 1 to 300 rows. Every row and column is nondecreasing; entries lie between -1000000000 and 1000000000.
1 <= k <= n*n. Count duplicate occurrences separately: this is the kth sorted value, not the kth distinct value.
Aim for less than O(n^2) auxiliary memory; the reference uses constant workspace.
hints: The number of cells <= a candidate value increases monotonically with that value.
Binary-search the value range, counting eligible cells by walking a staircase from the bottom-left.
If matrix[row][col]<=mid, add row+1 and move right; otherwise move up. Keep the smallest mid with count>=k.
Every staircase step removes a row or column, so each count costs O(n), and the first feasible value is the kth occurrence.
editorial: Binary-search between the minimum and maximum cell values. A bottom-left staircase counts values <= mid in O(n) without flattening or sorting the matrix. If the count is at least k, the answer is no larger than mid; otherwise it is larger. Duplicate cells contribute individually. The oracle flattens and sorts independently; generated matrices are row/column sorted but need not be row-major sorted.

tests.explanation: Sorted values are [1,5,9,10,11,12,13,13,15]. Both occurrences of 13 count, and position 8 is 13.
The only cell is the first smallest value, so return -5.
